column1: # Call-count fingerprint groups: NAME <TAB> REGEX
# One regex per logical component, matched against the symbol names in BOTH engines'
# callgrind profiles and the matches summed. Each row is the claim "zfish calls this as
# often as Stockfish does" -- a claim about the ALGORITHM, not about cost, and immune to
# inlining as long as the symbol survives on both sides.
# WHAT THIS CATCHES THAT NOTHING ELSE HERE DOES. Every other differential in this tree
# compares VALUES -- the bench anchor, the UCI goldens, arch-determinism, upstream-walk --
# and each one passes over a state divergence that happens not to move a node count on the
# positions it drives. The sibling C port had two real defects living behind that all-green
# wall (a `ucinewgame` that discarded the position, and a mate/stalemate root that skipped
# the per-worker reset), and BOTH surfaced here as one call of difference in set_check_info.
# zfish reads 165,082 -- upstream's value, so it has neither -- but the check is what
# proves that rather than the reading of two files.
# CHOOSE SYMBOLS THAT SURVIVE INLINING ON BOTH SIDES. A group whose regex matches nothing
# on one side is a MISS and fails, because a silent zero would read as agreement forever.
# If a compiler change inlines a symbol away, fix the row rather than deleting the check,
# and prefer a callee too big to inline over its caller. `isDraw` has no row for exactly
# this reason: zfish inlines it away entirely, so there is nothing to compare.
# MATCH ONE SYMBOL PER SIDE, AND VERIFY IT. A loose regex silently sums symbols that are
# not the same thing: `Position::do_move` alone also catches upstream's delegating 4-arg
# overload (250 calls) and reads as a 250-call divergence that is not there. Check a new
# row with `perf_fingerprint.py calls <out> --match ...` before trusting it.
